thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: prom-scrape-failure detected for cluster-prod-metrics — 3/5 scrape jobs failing, autopage triggered :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-4592 created and routed to oncall-sre (SEV2)
oncall-sre: ack. I’m on it, grabbing runbook and current graph links.
maria-ng: seeing missing `service.request_duration_seconds` for a bunch of services in grafana — dashboards show gaps starting ~21:30 UTC.
ajordan: log-ingest-queue consumer lag jumped to ~150k msgs, indexer backlog growing, raw logs delayed. Kafka consumer group offsets behind by ~200k.
kevin_h: rolling deploy of metrics-sidecar finished at 21:05 — could be related. Any correlate on node restarts?
oncall-sre: checking node events... nothing obvious from k8s. Querying prometheus targets: a lot of 504/timeout from prometheus-job-exporter on nodes in us-west-2.
maria-ng: customer support: two enterprise accounts reported missing alerts. Ticket #12345 opened. Potential customer impact = medium.
ajordan: running quick check: `kubectl get pods -n monitoring -o wide | grep exporter` -> a few exporters in CrashLoopBackOff on node-ip-12.
kevin_h: I can scale up the prometheus-scrape workers and bounce the exporter DaemonSet on affected nodes. Will that help?
oncall-sre: do that if we confirm exporter instability. Before restart, capture logs: `kubectl logs exporter-abc -n monitoring` — look for OOM or socket errors.
maria-ng: logs show repeated `read tcp 10.0.1.5:443: i/o timeout` then TLS handshake errors for some targets.
oncall-sre: seems network flakiness between prometheus and exporter. Also the log-ingest lag suggests Kafka broker network saturation or partitioning.
ajordan: checking kafka metrics: broker-2 outgoing bytes spike + increased request timeouts. Also see some GC pauses on indexer nodes.
oncall-sre: plan: 1) temporarily route prometheus scrape traffic to secondary scrape cluster (low-risk fallback); 2) scale kafka consumers by 2x to drain backlog; 3) bounce exporter pods on affected nodes; 4) open cloud provider ticket for network investigation.
kevin_h: implementing step 1: switching `scrape-routing` policy to prefer prom-secondary via feature flag `prom_fallback=true` (pushed).
maria-ng: confirming dashboards are refilling traces for `request_duration` — gaps shrinking.
ajordan: scaling consumers now: `kubectl scale deployment/log-consumer --replicas=6 -n logging`. Consumers are coming up. Lag down to 40k.
oncall-sre: good. I'll coordinate step 3, rolling restart of exporter DS in batches of 3 nodes to avoid mass disruption.
incident-bot: NOTE: oncall rotation change scheduled in 30m; oncall-sre please handoff if needed.
oncall-sre: thanks — will notify if escalation needed.
kevin_h: exporter pods show TLS handshake errors cleared after restart, no OOM, looks network-related.
maria-ng: customer tickets updated: two affected customers now report dashboards restored, alerts triggered as expected. Marking impact as reduced.
ajordan: log ingest lag down to 3k, indexer GC stabilized after bumping heap limit on indexer-1.
oncall-sre: re-running health checks on prometheus targets — 95% success. Will keep the prom_fallback flag for 15m to ensure stability.
kevin_h: opened CSP ticket with provider: case #CLOUD-8833 — they confirm transient network issues in us-west-2 region around 21:20 UTC.
oncall-sre: thanks. For now, marking incident as mitigated. Will let PagerDuty auto-resolve after we hit stable for 30m.
maria-ng: creating post-incident checklist: (a) investigate exporter TLS handshake root cause (b) consider retry/backoff on scraper (c) add consumer autoscaling policy for log-ingest (d) run a chaos test for network latency on monitoring nodes.
ajordan: adding runbook step to auto-scale consumers when lag > 50k for >10m.
oncall-sre: ack. I'll file a short postmortem and link runbook changes.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-4592 status -> mitigated (auto-resolve pending). :white_check_mark:
